newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann sees mobile phone profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann sees mobile phone profit rise.

text.p: Mannesmann Mobilfunk GmbH said on Wednesday it expects 1996 sales to total 4.2 billion marks, up 54 percent from last year, and a parallel increase in profit.
The Mannesmann AG unit's D2 mobile phone network had 2.3 million customers in December, up 850,000 this year.
In 1995, Mannesmann Mobilfunk showed a profit of 464 million marks.
Company president Juergen von Kuczkowski told a news conference he expects one in ten Germans will have a mobile phone connection by the end of 1997.

The company added 1,000 jobs in 1996 and expects to add a similar number next year, Kuczkowski said. It increased its investment in D2 expansion by 40 percent, bringing cumulative investment to 3.6 billion marks.

"The expansion as regards network coverage has been largely completed," the company said in a statement, adding that it would continue to invest in the capacity and quality of the network focusing on metropolitan and other busy areas.
The worldwide expansion of the GSM standard means D2 customers can now be reached in 46 countries, it said.
